q: You see a red sign with eight sides at an intersection, but snow covers the word on it. What must you do?
a: Come to a complete stop
b: Slow down and yield to cross traffic
c: Stop only if cross traffic is coming
d: Stop only if the sign also has an ALL WAY plaque
exp: The octagon shape is used only for the stop sign, so it means a full stop even when the word cannot be read.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2A.05 and Table 2A-1

q: What does a downward pointing triangle with a red border and a white center tell you to do?
a: Stop completely every time, then go
b: Keep your speed, because the other road must yield to you
c: Slow down and let traffic already in or near the intersection go first
d: Watch for a railroad crossing ahead
exp: That is the yield sign. You slow down, give the right of way, and may keep moving without a full stop if the way is clear.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Sections 2A.05 and 2B.05

q: A yellow horizontal rectangle shows one large black arrow pointing right. What does it mean?
a: A one way street begins to the right
b: The road turns sharply to the right, so slow down
c: Traffic must keep right of a divider
d: A side road joins from the right
exp: The Large Arrow sign is a yellow warning sign placed where the road makes a sharp turn in the direction of the arrow.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.10 (W1-6)

q: A yellow plaque reading 25 MPH sits under a curve warning sign. What does it show?
a: The legal speed limit for the whole road
b: The minimum speed allowed in the curve
c: The advised top speed for the curve in good conditions
d: The speed limit for trucks only
exp: This is an advisory speed plaque. It is advice for the curve, while the legal limit is posted on a white Speed Limit sign.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.59

q: A white rectangle reads DIVIDED HIGHWAY and shows two arrows pointing opposite ways, crossed by a vertical line. What does it tell you?
a: A median will begin on the road you are on
b: The divided highway ends and traffic becomes two way
c: Your road is a one way street
d: You are about to cross a divided highway, which has two separate roadways
exp: This regulatory sign stands on a road that meets a divided highway. Treat each roadway as its own street: traffic on the first comes from your left, on the second from your right.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.50 (R6-3)

q: What does an orange diamond shaped sign mean?
a: A school zone ahead
b: A general hazard such as a curve
c: Road work or temporary changes ahead
d: Services such as gas and food
exp: Orange is the color for temporary traffic control in work zones. Yellow is used for general warnings.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 6H.01

q: A yellow pennant shaped sign appears on the left side of the road. What does it mark?
a: A school crossing
b: A lane that ends ahead
c: A sharp curve to the left
d: The start of a no passing zone
exp: The pennant is used only for the No Passing Zone sign, and it stands on the left where you look before passing.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Table 2A-1 and Section 2C.53

q: On a freeway, a green sign over your lane has a yellow panel at the bottom that reads EXIT ONLY. What does it mean?
a: If you stay in this lane, you must take the exit
b: This is the last exit for several miles
c: Only trucks may use this exit
d: The exit is closed, so stay on the freeway
exp: A yellow EXIT ONLY panel marks a lane that leaves the freeway. Move out of it early if you want to stay on the freeway.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2E, EXIT ONLY panel (E11-1)

q: A flagger in a work zone turns the paddle so that SLOW faces you. What should you do?
a: Keep your normal speed, because only STOP needs action
b: Stop, then go when the flagger waves
c: Change lanes immediately
d: Move ahead slowly and watch for workers
exp: The SLOW face means you may proceed with caution through the work area.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 6D.05

q: A large lighted arrow board in a work zone shows an arrow flashing to the left. What should you do?
a: Stay in your lane, because the arrow is meant for work trucks
b: Merge left early and smoothly because the lane ahead is closed
c: Turn left at the next street
d: Move right, away from the side the arrow points to
exp: A flashing arrow on an arrow board means a lane is closed ahead and traffic must move in the direction of the arrow.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 6L.06

q: Which sign shape tells you a railroad crossing is ahead?
a: A yellow diamond
b: A round yellow sign
c: A yellow pennant
d: A white rectangle
exp: The circle is reserved for the railroad advance warning sign, placed before the tracks.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2A.05 and Table 2A-1

q: A fluorescent yellow-green sign with five sides, shaped like a house with a pointed roof, shows two walking children. What does it warn you about?
a: A school zone or school crossing
b: A railroad crossing
c: A pedestrian crossing ahead
d: A playground near the road
exp: The pentagon is reserved for school signs.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2A.05 and Table 2A-1

q: Which color is used on signs that point you to gas, food, lodging and hospitals?
a: Green
b: Blue
c: Brown
d: Orange
exp: Blue guide signs show motorist services.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2A.06 and Table 2A-2

q: A brown sign most likely points you to which place?
a: A rest area with fuel
b: A highway exit
c: A hospital
d: A state park or historic site
exp: Brown signs guide drivers to recreation and cultural interest areas such as parks and historic sites.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2A.06 and Table 2A-2

q: What does a fluorescent pink sign that reads INCIDENT AHEAD tell you?
a: A crash or emergency scene is ahead
b: A school zone starts here
c: Road work is ahead
d: A police checkpoint is ahead
exp: Fluorescent pink is used for incident management signs at crash and emergency scenes.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 6H.01

q: Which statement about regulatory signs is correct?
a: They only suggest a safe speed
b: They state a law you must obey
c: They point to services and exits
d: They warn of hazards but carry no legal force
exp: Regulatory signs, such as Stop, Speed Limit and One Way, give rules that can be enforced.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2B

q: Most warning signs have what shape and color?
a: A white rectangle with black letters
b: A green rectangle with white letters
c: A yellow diamond with black symbols or words
d: A red circle with a white bar
exp: Warning signs are generally yellow diamonds with a black legend and border.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.02

q: Most guide signs on highways, showing exits and distances, are what color?
a: Yellow with black letters
b: Orange with black letters
c: Brown with white letters
d: Green with white letters
exp: Green is the color for direction and destination guide signs.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2A.06 and Table 2A-2

q: You are driving and pass a red rectangle sign with white letters reading WRONG WAY facing you. What does it mean?
a: You are driving against traffic and must safely turn around
b: Traffic ahead is merging from the left
c: The road ahead is closed for repairs
d: Oncoming traffic will share your lane ahead
exp: A Wrong Way sign faces drivers who have entered a one way road or ramp in the wrong direction.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.47

q: Where are you most likely to see a Do Not Enter sign?
a: At the start of a school zone
b: At the exit end of a freeway ramp
c: Before a sharp curve
d: At a rest area entrance
exp: Do Not Enter signs stand where traffic may not go in from that direction, such as freeway exit ramps and the far end of one way streets.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.46

q: Which sign shows the maximum legal speed on a road?
a: A yellow square plaque under a warning sign
b: An orange diamond
c: A yellow diamond with a number
d: A white rectangle with black numbers
exp: Speed Limit signs are white regulatory signs. Yellow speed plaques are advisory only.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.21

q: What is the difference between a Merge sign and a Lane Ends sign?
a: Merge means traffic is joining your road; Lane Ends means your road is losing a lane
b: They mean the same thing
c: Merge means your lane ends; Lane Ends means traffic joins from a ramp
d: Merge appears only on freeways; Lane Ends only on city streets
exp: A Merge sign warns that traffic will enter from another road, while a Lane Ends sign warns that one lane is about to end.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Sections 2C.45 and 2C.47

q: A yellow sign shows two arrows, one pointing up and one pointing down. What does it warn you about?
a: A divided highway begins
b: Two way traffic is ahead
c: You must make a U-turn
d: The road splits into two lanes going your way
exp: The Two Way Traffic sign warns that you are leaving a one way or divided road and oncoming traffic is ahead.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.51

q: What does a Divided Highway Ends sign tell you?
a: A median will soon separate the two directions
b: You are entering a one way street
c: Traffic will soon travel in both directions with no median between you
d: The right lane ends ahead
exp: When a divided highway ends, oncoming traffic is no longer separated from you by a divider.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.21

q: What does a School Speed Limit sign with a WHEN FLASHING plaque mean?
a: The school limit applies all day on school days
b: Slow down only if children are in the crosswalk
c: You must stop when the lights flash
d: The lower school limit applies while the yellow lights on the sign are flashing
exp: A WHEN FLASHING plaque means the reduced school limit is in force only while the sign's yellow beacons are flashing.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 7B.05 and Figure 7B-1

q: A school sign has a small plaque below it with an arrow pointing down at an angle. What does it mark?
a: The school crossing itself
b: The end of the school zone
c: A school bus stop two miles ahead
d: A parking area for parents
exp: The school sign with a diagonal downward arrow plaque marks the location of the school crosswalk.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 7B.03

q: A crossing guard in a school zone holds up a STOP paddle. What should you do?
a: Slow down and drive around the children
b: Stop and wait until the guard signals you to go
c: Stop only if a child is in your lane
d: Stop until the children reach the curb, then go without waiting for the guard
exp: Crossing guards stand in the road to stop all traffic, and drivers obey them like a stop sign.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 7D.02

q: When does a school zone end?
a: When you can no longer see the school building
b: When you pass the school crossing
c: When you pass the End School Zone sign
d: As soon as no children are in sight
exp: Where one is posted, an End School Zone sign marks the downstream end of the zone. Keep the school limit until you pass it.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 7B.02

q: In a work zone, a flagger's signal and a nearby sign seem to give different directions. Whose directions do you follow?
a: The flagger's
b: The sign's
c: The traffic signal's, if one is working
d: The flagger's, but only in daylight
exp: A flagger controls traffic as it is right now, so the flagger's directions come first inside the work zone.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 6D.05

q: Drums, cones, vertical panels and barricades in a work zone are known as what?
a: Delineators that mark the edge of a curve
b: Barriers that mean the road is closed to all traffic
c: Channeling devices that guide you through the zone
d: Signs that show detour distances
exp: These orange and white devices guide traffic along a safe path and keep drivers out of the work area.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Part 6

q: An Interstate route has an even number, such as 80. Which way does it usually run?
a: It runs mostly north and south
b: It loops around a city
c: It is a toll road
d: It runs mostly east and west
exp: Interstates with even numbers run mostly east and west; odd numbers run mostly north and south.
src: FHWA, Interstate route numbering, https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/highwayhistory/data/page07.cfm

q: A yellow diamond sign shows a car with two wavy marks behind it. What does it mean?
a: The road has sharp curves
b: Loose gravel is falling from trucks
c: The road is slippery when wet
d: The road ahead is under repair
exp: This is the Slippery When Wet sign. Slow down in rain and avoid sudden braking or steering.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.30

q: Why do stop, yield and railroad signs have shapes that no other sign may use?
a: Because these signs are larger than all others
b: Because these are the only signs the law requires you to obey
c: Because only these signs may use the color red
d: So drivers can recognize them from the shape alone, even at night or when the words are covered
exp: Reserved shapes let drivers identify the most important signs from a distance and from behind.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2A.05 and Table 2A-1

q: A yellow horizontal rectangle shows one black arrow with a head at each end, pointing left and right. What does it mean?
a: Two way traffic is ahead
b: Your road ends ahead; you must turn left or right
c: You may pass on either side of a slow vehicle
d: A lane is added on each side
exp: The Two-Direction Large Arrow stands at the end of a road, such as at a T intersection, to show you must turn one way or the other.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.43 (W1-7)

q: A yellow diamond shows a smoothly bent arrow that swings one way and then the other, like an S. What does it warn you about?
a: Two curves in opposite directions
b: A road joining from the side
c: A lane that ends
d: Two way traffic
exp: This is the Reverse Curve sign: the road bends one way and then back the other way.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2C, Reverse Curve sign (W1-4)

q: A yellow diamond shows an arrow with two right angle bends, one to the left and one to the right. How is it different from a sign with a smoothly bent arrow?
a: It marks a gentle bend you can take at the speed limit
b: It means the road is closed ahead
c: It warns of sharper turns that need a slower speed
d: It marks a detour route
exp: Right angle arrows are turn signs, used where the bend is sharp enough that the safe speed is low. Smooth arrows are curve signs.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2C, Turn and Reverse Turn signs (W1-1, W1-3)

q: A yellow diamond shows a straight vertical black line with a shorter line joining it from the right side. What does it warn you about?
a: A right turn lane ahead
b: A side road joins from the right, so watch for turning or entering cars
c: Your lane ends on the right
d: A no passing zone on the right
exp: The Side Road sign shows where another road enters, so vehicles may turn in front of you or pull out.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.41 (W2-2)

q: A yellow diamond shows a black symbol shaped like the letter Y. What does it warn you about?
a: A railroad crossing
b: Two lanes merging into one
c: A yield sign ahead
d: The road splits into two roads
exp: The Y Intersection sign warns that the road divides ahead and you will have to choose a branch.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.41 (W2-5)

q: A yellow diamond shows three curved arrows chasing each other in a circle. What is ahead?
a: A circular intersection, or roundabout
b: A U-turn area
c: A traffic signal
d: A turnaround area for trucks
exp: The Circular Intersection sign warns of a roundabout. Slow down and yield to traffic already in the circle.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2C, Circular Intersection sign (W2-6)

q: A yellow diamond shows a truck tipping over below a curved arrow. What does it warn about?
a: A truck weigh station
b: A truck route that crosses the road
c: A curve where tall trucks have tipped over, so slow down
d: Trucks may not use this road
exp: The Truck Rollover sign is posted before curves where trucks risk tipping and comes with an advisory speed plaque.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.11 (W1-13)

q: A yellow diamond reads NARROW BRIDGE. What should you do?
a: Stop before the bridge and wait for oncoming traffic to clear
b: Stop and wait for a flagger
c: Move toward the center line to stay off the edge
d: Slow down and expect less room than on the road
exp: The bridge ahead is narrower than the road leading to it. Slow down, keep right and watch oncoming traffic.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.18 (W5-2)

q: A yellow diamond reads ONE LANE BRIDGE. A car coming the other way is already on the bridge. What should you do?
a: Wait and let it cross first
b: Cross at the same time, keeping to the right
c: Go first if you reached the sign before the other car reached the bridge
d: Cross quickly before it reaches the middle
exp: A one lane bridge has room for only one vehicle at a time. Let a vehicle already on it finish crossing.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.19 (W5-3)

q: A yellow diamond reads LOW SHOULDER. What does it warn about?
a: The speed limit drops ahead
b: The shoulder is a little lower than the road surface
c: The shoulder is wide enough to drive on
d: Low branches hang over the road
exp: Low Shoulder warns of a small step down from the pavement to the shoulder, about 3 inches or less.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.29 (W8-9)

q: A yellow diamond shows a car tilting off the edge of the road, with a yellow plaque below it. What does the sign warn about?
a: A slippery road
b: A steep hill
c: A road that floods
d: A shoulder that drops off sharply from the road edge
exp: The Shoulder Drop-Off sign warns that the edge of the pavement drops more than 3 inches to the shoulder.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.29 (W8-17, W8-17P)

q: A yellow diamond shows a horse pulling a buggy. What should you expect?
a: Slow horse-drawn vehicles on the road
b: A horse trail where riders cross the road
c: A farm equipment crossing
d: A livestock crossing
exp: This sign warns that slow horse-drawn vehicles use the road. Slow down and give them plenty of room (Chapter 9).
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.54 (W11-14)

q: At the entrance to a street, a yellow diamond reads DEAD END. What does it mean?
a: The street is closed for repairs
b: Traffic on the street must stop
c: The street ends with no way through
d: The street is one way
exp: A Dead End sign marks a street that ends without meeting another street, so you will have to turn around.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2C, DEAD END sign (W14-1)

q: A yellow diamond at the entrance to a neighborhood reads NO OUTLET. What does it mean?
a: You may not park on these streets
b: The streets inside have no other way out
c: Only residents may enter
d: Through trucks are not allowed
exp: No Outlet means the road or group of streets ahead has only one way in and out.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2C, NO OUTLET sign (W14-2)

q: Next to a traffic signal, a white sign reads LEFT TURN YIELD ON and shows a green circle. What does it tell you?
a: Left turns are not allowed on green
b: Left turns are protected when the light is green
c: Wait for a green arrow before turning left
d: On a green ball you may turn left, but you must yield to oncoming traffic
exp: On a round green light the left turn is not protected. The sign reminds you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.59 (R10-12)

q: A stop sign has a white plaque under it that reads EXCEPT RIGHT TURN. You are turning right. What does the plaque mean?
a: You do not have to stop to turn right, but you still yield as needed
b: Only drivers turning right must stop
c: Right turns are not allowed
d: You may turn right only on a green light
exp: The plaque exempts drivers turning right from the stop. Everyone going straight or left must still stop.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.04 (R1-10P)

q: A yield sign has a white plaque under it that reads TO ONCOMING TRAFFIC. Where are you most likely to see it?
a: At a freeway on ramp
b: At a school crossing
c: At a one lane bridge
d: At a railroad crossing
exp: The plaque tells drivers going straight to yield to vehicles coming toward them, such as where a bridge has only one lane.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.18 (R1-2aP)

q: A white sign shows two curved arrows pointing opposite ways, one turning left at the top and one at the bottom, with the word ONLY. What does it mean?
a: The center lane is for left turns only, from both directions
b: Traffic may turn around here
c: Only buses may use the center lane
d: The road is one way in both lanes
exp: This sign marks a shared center turn lane, used only for left turns by drivers from both directions (Chapter 3).
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.32 (R3-9b)

q: An orange diamond shows a person holding a paddle on a pole. What should you do?
a: Prepare to merge, because a lane is closed ahead
b: Slow down and be ready to stop for a flagger ahead
c: Look for a school crossing guard
d: Change lanes to the left
exp: The Flagger symbol sign warns that a flagger is controlling traffic ahead. Slow down and follow the paddle.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Part 6, Flagger symbol sign (W20-7)

q: An orange diamond shows a person digging with a shovel. What does it mean?
a: A detour begins here
b: The road ahead is closed
c: Loose gravel is on the road
d: People are working on or near the road
exp: The Workers sign warns that people are working close to traffic. Slow down and yield to them.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Part 6, Worker symbol sign (W21-1)

q: An orange diamond reads RIGHT LANE CLOSED AHEAD. What is the best response?
a: Stay in the right lane until the cones
b: Move to the shoulder
c: Merge left early and smoothly
d: Stop and wait for a flagger
exp: The sign gives you time to merge before the closure. Merging early keeps traffic moving and avoids last second lane changes.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Part 6, Lane Closed sign (W20-5)

q: An orange rectangle reads DETOUR and shows a black arrow pointing right. What does it mean?
a: Follow the marked route because the usual road is closed
b: Right turns are not allowed
c: A rest area is to the right
d: The right lane is for trucks
exp: Detour signs guide you around a closed road. Follow the orange DETOUR arrows until you rejoin your route.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Part 6, Detour signs (W20-2, M4-9)

q: An orange rectangle reads END ROAD WORK. What does it tell you?
a: Road work starts here
b: Road work continues for one more mile
c: The work zone has ended
d: The road is closed beyond this point
exp: END ROAD WORK marks the end of the work zone. Keep the work zone speed until you pass it.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Part 6, END ROAD WORK sign (G20-2)

q: A round yellow sign shows a black X and the letters R and R. What is ahead?
a: A right lane reduction ahead
b: A railroad crossing
c: A crossroad
d: A road repair area
exp: The round railroad advance warning sign stands before the tracks. Slow down, look and listen.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2A.05 and Part 8 (W10-1)

q: A white X-shaped sign reads RAILROAD CROSSING. How should you treat it?
a: As a stop sign, every time
b: As a warning only, with no duty to slow down
c: As a yield sign: slow down, look, and stop for any train
d: As a sign you may ignore if no gates are down
exp: The crossbuck is treated like a yield sign. Never start across unless you can clear the tracks completely.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Part 8, Crossbuck sign (R15-1)

q: A square sign shows a red circle with a white horizontal bar across it. What does it mean?
a: Do not enter the road from this direction
b: No parking
c: Stop ahead
d: Road closed for repairs
exp: Do Not Enter stands at the exit end of ramps and the far end of one way streets.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.46 (R5-1)

q: A yellow diamond shows a straight arrow with a curved line joining it from the right. What should you do?
a: Move right to let the other lane end
b: Watch for traffic joining your road and make room
c: Stop for cross traffic
d: Turn right ahead
exp: This is the Merge sign. Traffic from the side will enter your lane, so adjust your speed or position to let it in.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2C, Merge sign (W4-1)

q: A yellow diamond shows two lines, with the right one bending in toward the left one. What does it mean?
a: A side road joins from the right
b: A narrow bridge
c: The right lane ends, so its drivers must merge left
d: A curve to the left
exp: The Lane Ends sign warns that one lane is about to end. Drivers in it must merge into the next lane.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2C, Lane Ends sign (W4-2)

q: A yellow diamond shows a traffic light with red, yellow and green lamps. What does it mean?
a: A signal is ahead, possibly out of sight, so be ready to stop
b: The signal ahead is broken
c: Pedestrians may cross here
d: A railroad signal is ahead
exp: The Signal Ahead sign warns of a traffic signal hidden by a curve or hill. Start slowing in time.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2C, Signal Ahead sign (W3-3)

q: An orange diamond reads ROAD WORK AHEAD. When should you slow down?
a: When you see the first worker
b: Only if a flagger signals you
c: When you reach the first cones or barrels
d: Now, at the first orange sign
exp: Work zone signs give you time to slow down before you reach the work. Slow down at the first one.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Part 6, ROAD WORK AHEAD sign (W20-1)

q: A yellow diamond shows two lines that come together around a black rounded shape at the bottom of the sign. What does it warn about?
a: The road splits around a median
b: A side road
c: A low clearance ahead
d: The divided highway ends and oncoming traffic will be beside you
exp: The Divided Highway Ends sign warns that the median ends ahead and traffic will travel both ways with no divider.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.21 (W6-2)

q: You come to a road that crosses a divided highway with a wide median. You want to turn left onto the highway. What should you do?
a: Turn left into the first roadway you reach
b: Cross the first roadway and the median, then turn left onto the second roadway
c: Wait in the median facing oncoming traffic on the first roadway
d: Turn right, then make a U-turn on the first roadway
exp: Each roadway is a separate one way street. The first carries traffic from your left, so a left turn is made onto the second roadway.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.50 (R6-3); Uniform Vehicle Code 11-311 (divided highways)

q: In a work zone, the lanes are separated by a solid white line. What should you do?
a: Stay in your lane
b: Change lanes whenever traffic is light
c: Use the shoulder to pass slow cars
d: Change lanes only to pass a slow work vehicle
exp: A solid white line tells you to stay in your lane. In a work zone, lane changes are a common cause of crashes.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 3A (a solid lane line discourages crossing); Part 6

q: A slow line painting truck is working in your lane, with an arrow board on the back. No flagger or sign tells you to pass. What should you do?
a: Pass it quickly on the shoulder
b: Pass it on the left as soon as you can
c: Pass it on the right if the right lane is open
d: Stay behind it and do not pass
exp: Do not pass a moving work operation unless a flagger or sign directs you to. Workers may step out around it.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Part 6 (mobile operations)

q: You stop at a stop line, but parked trucks block your view of the cross street. What should you do next?
a: Go, because you already stopped
b: Honk and go
c: Creep forward slowly until you can see, then go when it is clear
d: Wait at the stop line until the trucks move
exp: Stop first at the line. If you still cannot see, edge forward slowly until you can, and go only when the way is clear.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2B, STOP sign (R1-1); Uniform Vehicle Code 11-403

q: Which group of people must you yield to in a work zone?
a: Only police officers
b: Workers, flaggers and work vehicles
c: Only workers wearing hard hats
d: Only flaggers holding a STOP paddle
exp: Inside a work zone, yield to workers and flaggers and to work vehicles entering or leaving the work area.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Part 6 (flaggers and worker safety)

q: A yellow plaque under a shoulder warning sign reads SHOULDER DROP-OFF. How big is the drop it warns about?
a: About 1 inch
b: More than 3 inches
c: More than 6 inches
d: More than 12 inches
exp: The drop-off sign is used where the pavement edge drops more than 3 inches. Low Shoulder covers smaller steps.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2C.29 (W8-9, W8-17)

q: A tall yellow panel with black stripes sloping down to the right is fixed to a concrete support in the road. What does it tell you?
a: Pass on the left side of the support
b: A lane ends on the right
c: Pass on the right side of the support
d: A work zone starts here
exp: This is an object marker. Its stripes slope down toward the side you should pass on, here the right.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., object markers (OM3-L, OM3-R)

q: A plain red diamond-shaped sign stands where the pavement stops. What does it mark?
a: The end of the road; you must stop or turn
b: A stop sign is ahead
c: A dangerous curve
d: A no passing zone begins
exp: A red diamond, or a group of red reflectors, is an end of roadway marker: the road ends there.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., end of roadway markers (OM4-1)

q: A white square sign shows a black bicycle inside a red circle with a red slash. What does it mean?
a: A bike lane begins
b: Watch for cyclists crossing
c: Bicycles must ride on the sidewalk
d: Bicycles may not use this road
exp: A red circle and slash forbids what is shown inside it. This sign bans bicycles from the road.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B (R5-6)

q: A green freeway sign has its exit number tab on the left edge, with a yellow panel reading LEFT. What does it tell you?
a: The exit leaves from the right lane
b: The exit leaves from the left side, so you will need the left lane
c: The left lane ends ahead
d: Left turns are allowed at the end of the ramp
exp: An exit number tab on the left side of the sign, with a yellow LEFT panel, marks an exit that leaves from the left.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2E (exit number plaques, E1-5bP)

q: A small white plate reading JCT sits above a route marker. What does it mean?
a: The route ends here
b: You are already on that route
c: A junction with that route is ahead
d: A truck route begins
exp: JCT stands for junction: the plate tells you that you are coming to a junction with the route shown below it.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 2D (M2-1 junction auxiliary sign)

q: You want to turn left and see a flashing yellow arrow. What must you do?
a: Turn right away, because oncoming traffic is stopped
b: Turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
c: Stop and wait for a green arrow
d: Treat it like a stop sign: stop, then turn
exp: A flashing yellow arrow permits the turn, but oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield first.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4A.04

q: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?
a: Slow down and go ahead with caution
b: Treat it as a yield sign and slow down
c: Stop only if cross traffic is coming
d: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe, as at a stop sign
exp: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4A.04

q: Your light turns steady yellow as you approach the intersection, and you have room to stop safely before the stop line. What should you do?
a: Speed up so you clear the intersection before the red
b: Keep going, because a yellow light still lets you enter
c: Stop only if a car is waiting on the cross street
d: Stop before the stop line
exp: A steady yellow means the green is ending and red comes next. Stop if you can do it safely.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4A.03

q: You reach an intersection where the traffic signal is completely dark because of a power failure. What should you do?
a: Treat it as an all way stop
b: Treat it as a flashing yellow light and slow down
c: Stop only if cross traffic is coming
d: Go through without stopping if you are on the busier road
exp: A dark signal is handled like an all way stop: stop, take turns, and go when it is safe.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 4 (traffic signals); California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (traffic signals)

q: On a two lane road, a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line run side by side. The broken line is on your side. What may you do?
a: Never pass
b: Pass only to turn left into a driveway
c: Pass when it is safe
d: Pass only on the right
exp: You may pass only from the side with the broken line, and only when it is safe.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Sections 3A.04 and 3B.01

q: Driving at night, you notice the solid yellow line is on your right and a white line is on your left on a divided highway. What does this tell you?
a: You are in the far left lane, where passing is allowed
b: You are in the correct lane
c: You are driving the wrong way
d: You are in a shared center turn lane
exp: On a one way road or divided highway, the yellow line belongs on your left. If it is on your right, you are going against traffic.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Sections 3A.03 and 3B.09

q: You are waiting to turn right. The pedestrian signal shows a flashing raised hand, and a person is halfway across the street in front of you. What should you do?
a: Wait until the person is out of your path
b: Turn as soon as the person is past the middle of the street
c: Creep into the crosswalk so you are ready to turn
d: Turn, because the flashing hand means the person must stop
exp: The flashing hand tells people not to start crossing. Someone already crossing keeps going, and you must yield.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4A.06

q: What is a shared center turn lane used for?
a: Starting a left turn a block or more before the turn
b: Waiting to turn right into a driveway
c: Left turns by drivers from both directions
d: Passing slow vehicles
exp: A two way left turn lane is only for left turns, never for passing or travel.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 3B.05

q: What do yellow lines on the road separate?
a: Parking spaces from travel lanes
b: Traffic moving in opposite directions
c: Lanes moving in the same direction
d: Bike lanes from car lanes
exp: Yellow lines separate opposing traffic. White lines separate lanes going the same way.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 3A.03

q: You stop at a steady red light and want to turn right. There is no sign about turning. What may you do?
a: Turn right only if a green arrow appears
b: Turn right after the complete stop, once pedestrians and traffic with a green light have gone
c: Turn right without stopping if no one is coming
d: Wait for the light to turn green before turning
exp: A right turn on red is allowed after a full stop unless a sign forbids it, and you must yield first.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4A.03

q: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
a: Slow down and go ahead with caution
b: Only turning traffic may go
c: Stop and wait for a green light
d: The light is about to turn red
exp: Flashing yellow works like a caution sign. You do not have to stop, but you must watch for traffic and pedestrians.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4A.04

q: A steady green arrow pointing left is lit. What does it tell you?
a: You must turn left from every lane
b: You may turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic
c: The left turn is about to end
d: You may turn left; traffic that would cross your path is stopped
exp: A green arrow gives a protected turn. You still yield to anyone already in the intersection.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4A.03

q: What does a steady yellow arrow mean?
a: Oncoming traffic must stop for you
b: Turns are not allowed at this intersection
c: You may turn after yielding to oncoming traffic
d: The protected turn shown by the arrow is ending
exp: A steady yellow arrow warns that the green arrow movement is ending and a red arrow or other change is coming.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4A.03

q: Where must you stop for a steady red light when there is no stop line painted?
a: Right at the corner, with your front wheels in the crosswalk
b: Just past the crosswalk, so you can see cross traffic
c: Wherever your front bumper lines up with the signal pole
d: Before the crosswalk, or before the intersection if there is no crosswalk
exp: Without a stop line, you stop before the crosswalk; without a crosswalk, before entering the intersection.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4A.03

q: Your light is green, but a police officer directing traffic signals you to stop. What should you do?
a: Stop, because the officer's directions override the signal
b: Keep going, because the green light gives you the right of way
c: Stop only if cross traffic is coming
d: Slow down and go around the officer
exp: A person legally directing traffic overrides signals, signs and markings.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 4 (traffic officers)

q: Traffic ahead is backed up past the intersection and your light is green. What should you do?
a: Enter the intersection and wait there
b: Wait before the intersection until there is room to get all the way through
c: Turn on your hazard lights and go
d: Drive onto the shoulder to get around
exp: A green light does not let you block the intersection. Enter only when you can clear it.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (right of way)

q: What does a steady red X over a lane mean?
a: The lane is for left turns only
b: Do not drive in that lane
c: You may drive in the lane with caution
d: Leave the lane soon, it is closing
exp: A steady red X is a lane control signal that closes the lane to you.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4T.02 (lane-use control signals); MUTCD 2009 ed., Section 4M.02

q: A steady yellow X is lit over your lane. What should you do?
a: Speed up to clear the lane
b: Stop in the lane until it turns green
c: Get ready to move out of the lane safely, because it is about to close
d: Stay in the lane, it is now reserved for you
exp: A steady yellow X warns that the lane is about to close and will change to a red X.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4T.02 (lane-use control signals); MUTCD 2009 ed., Section 4M.02

q: What does a green arrow pointing down at a lane mean?
a: The lane is for buses only
b: Turn left from that lane
c: The lane ends ahead
d: You may drive in that lane
exp: A downward green arrow over a lane is the lane control signal that opens the lane.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4T.02 (lane-use control signals); MUTCD 2009 ed., Section 4M.02

q: What is the purpose of a ramp meter on a freeway on ramp?
a: To measure your speed before the freeway
b: To let cars onto the freeway one at a time so merging stays smooth
c: To show the freeway speed limit
d: To close the ramp at night
exp: A ramp meter spaces out cars entering the freeway. Stop on red and go on green.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Chapter 4P (traffic control signals for freeway entrance ramps)

q: On a pedestrian signal, what does the walking person symbol mean?
a: Drivers may turn without checking the crosswalk
b: The crossing is closed
c: People may start to cross the street
d: People must not enter the street
exp: The walking person means pedestrians may begin crossing in the direction of the signal.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4A.06

q: What does the countdown number on a pedestrian signal show?
a: The seconds left for people to finish crossing
b: How many people may cross at once
c: The seconds until the light turns green for you
d: The seconds until the walk signal comes back
exp: The countdown shows how much crossing time remains while the hand flashes.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4I.04 (pedestrian countdown); California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (pedestrian signals)

q: What do white lines between lanes tell you?
a: Traffic in those lanes moves in the same direction
b: The lanes are reserved for buses
c: Passing is never allowed
d: Traffic in those lanes moves in opposite directions
exp: White lane lines separate lanes of traffic going the same way.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 3A.03

q: What does a double solid yellow center line mean?
a: Passing allowed only for traffic on the right
b: Passing allowed from either side when safe
c: The road is one way
d: No passing for traffic in either direction
exp: A double solid yellow line prohibits passing from both sides.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 3B.01

q: When may you cross a double solid yellow line?
a: To turn left into or out of a driveway or side road
b: Whenever no oncoming traffic is in sight
c: To pass a slow vehicle
d: To pass a line of cars on a hill
exp: You may not cross a double solid yellow line to pass, but you may cross it to make a left turn into or out of a driveway or road.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 4 (pavement markings)

q: What does a solid white line between two lanes going your way mean?
a: Change lanes freely
b: Stay in your lane unless you must change lanes
c: The lane ends ahead
d: The lanes go in opposite directions
exp: A solid white lane line discourages lane changes. A broken white line permits them when safe.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 3B.06

q: How is a reversible lane marked?
a: With a single solid white line on each side
b: With a double broken yellow line on each side
c: With a double solid yellow line on each side
d: With white diamond symbols
exp: Reversible lanes use double broken yellow lines and are controlled by signs or overhead lane signals.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 3B.04

q: What does a row of white triangles painted across your lane, pointing toward you, mean?
a: Speed bumps ahead
b: Railroad crossing ahead
c: Yield line: if you must yield, stop behind it
d: The lane ends ahead
exp: Shark teeth are a yield line and go with a yield sign.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 3B.19

q: A large X with the letters RR is painted across your lane. What does it mean?
a: A railroad crossing is ahead
b: Rough road ahead
c: A crossroad ahead
d: Road repair ahead
exp: The RXR pavement marking warns of a railroad crossing ahead.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 8C.02

q: A white arrow curving left is painted in your lane with the word ONLY. What does it mean?
a: Left turns are allowed only at rush hour
b: You may turn left or go straight
c: Traffic in this lane must turn left
d: Left turns are not allowed
exp: ONLY with an arrow marks a mandatory turn lane.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 3B.21

q: Beside the signal, a white sign reads LEFT TURN YIELD ON and shows a green circle. The round green light is on. What may you do?
a: Turn left at once, because oncoming traffic is stopped
b: Wait for a green arrow before turning left
c: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
d: Turn left only after the light turns yellow
exp: A round green light allows the left turn, but it is not protected. The sign reminds you to yield first.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.59 (R10-12); Section 4A.03

q: A flashing yellow X is lit over a lane in the middle of the street. What may you use the lane for?
a: Passing slow cars
b: Driving straight in either direction
c: Nothing; the lane is closed
d: Making a left turn
exp: A flashing yellow X over a center lane means the lane may be used only to make a left turn, with care.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 4T.02 (lane-use control signals)

q: An ambulance with its siren on and lights flashing is coming up behind you. What should you do?
a: Stop where you are in your lane
b: Slow down and keep going in the right lane
c: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop
d: Move to the left lane so it can pass on the right
exp: For an approaching emergency vehicle, pull to the right edge and stop until it passes.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (emergency vehicles)

q: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and its stop arm out. When may you go?
a: When you see no children near the bus
b: As soon as the doors close
c: When the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm folds in
d: When the children have reached the sidewalk
exp: Stay stopped until the red lights go off and the stop arm folds in; children can still be crossing after the doors close.
src: NHTSA, School Bus Safety, https://www.nhtsa.gov/road-safety/school-bus-safety

q: You and another driver reach a four way stop at the same moment. The other car is on your right. Who goes first?
a: You, because the car on the left goes first
b: The car on your right
c: Whichever driver signals first
d: The car on the wider road
exp: When two cars at right angles stop at the same time, the car on the right goes first.
src: California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (right of way)

q: You and an oncoming car stop at a four way stop at the same time. You want to turn left and the other driver is going straight. Who goes first?
a: You, because you signaled first
b: You, because a left turn clears the intersection quickly
c: Both cars go at the same time
d: The oncoming car going straight
exp: A driver turning left yields to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (right of way)

q: A fire truck with its siren on has just passed you while you were stopped at the right edge of the road. What should you do before pulling back into traffic?
a: Check for a second emergency vehicle, then pull out and stay well back
b: Pull out right away and follow close behind it through traffic
c: Pull out at once so you do not hold up the cars behind you
d: Wait until you can no longer hear the siren, then speed up to make up time
exp: Another emergency vehicle may be coming behind the first, and you must never follow one closely. Check traffic, then pull out and stay well back.
src: Uniform Vehicle Code (NCUTLO) 11-405 and 11-1107; New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (emergency vehicles)

q: You approach an intersection with no signs or signals, and another car arrives from the left at about the same time. Who should yield?
a: Both cars must stop and wait
b: The other car, because you are on its right
c: You, because the other car is on your left
d: The car going straight, whichever side it is on
exp: At an uncontrolled intersection, when two cars arrive together, you let the car on your right go first.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (right of way)

q: You are leaving a parking lot and want to enter the street. Who must you yield to?
a: Only traffic in the lane you plan to enter
b: Only traffic coming from your left
c: Pedestrians on the sidewalk and all traffic on the street
d: Only pedestrians, because street traffic must slow for you
exp: Drivers entering a road from a driveway or lot yield to pedestrians and to road traffic.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (right of way)

q: You are in the middle of an intersection when you hear a fire truck siren behind you. What should you do?
a: Turn left to get out of the way
b: Stop right away in the intersection
c: Back up out of the intersection
d: Drive through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop
exp: Stopping in the intersection blocks the emergency vehicle. Clear it first, then pull over.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (emergency vehicles)

q: A school bus ahead of you turns on flashing yellow lights. What does this mean?
a: You may pass the bus quickly before it stops
b: Children have finished getting off
c: Traffic may pass on the left with care
d: The bus is about to stop; slow down and get ready to stop
exp: Flashing yellow lights warn that the bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children.
src: NHTSA, School Bus Safety, https://www.nhtsa.gov/road-safety/school-bus-safety

q: A pedestrian with a white cane is waiting to cross in front of you. What should you do?
a: Stop and wait until the person has crossed
b: Drive around the person slowly
c: Honk to let the person know you are there
d: Call out to tell the person to cross
exp: People using a white cane or guide dog always get the right-of-way. Honking can confuse them.
src: California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (right of way)

q: At an all way stop, who goes first when the cars arrived at different times?
a: The car on the left
b: The car that came to a stop first
c: The car turning right
d: The car on the busier road
exp: At an all way stop, the order is first to stop, first to go.
src: California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (right of way)

q: What does it mean to yield the right-of-way?
a: Stop and wait until no other car is in sight
b: Let other road users go first, slowing or stopping if needed
c: Always come to a complete stop
d: Signal so the other driver knows to wait
exp: Yielding means letting others go first. You stop only if someone is coming.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (right of way)

q: Another driver should yield to you but keeps coming into the intersection. What should you do?
a: Speed up so you get through first
b: Let the other driver go to avoid a crash
c: Honk and hold your position
d: Keep going, because you have the right-of-way
exp: The law only says who must yield. You must still do everything you can to avoid a crash.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (right of way)

q: You are turning left on a green light with no arrow. A car is coming toward you going straight. What should you do?
a: Wait for the oncoming car to pass, then turn when safe
b: Turn, because left turners have the right-of-way
c: Stop and back up
d: Turn quickly before it reaches you
exp: Left turners yield to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (right of way)

q: You are on a road that ends at a T intersection with no signs. Who has the right-of-way?
a: The driver on the left
b: You, because you got there first
c: Traffic on the through road
d: Whichever driver is turning left
exp: At a T intersection without signs, traffic on the road that continues goes first.
src: California Driver Handbook, Navigating the Roads (T intersections)

q: You want to turn left into a driveway in the middle of a block. What must you do first?
a: Pull onto the shoulder
b: Stop and turn on your hazard lights
c: Yield to oncoming traffic
d: Wait for a green arrow
exp: When turning left into a driveway or parking lot, you yield to oncoming traffic, even with no sign or signal.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (right of way)

q: You are turning right on a green light. What should you check for?
a: Pedestrians in the crosswalk and bicycles or motorcycles beside you
b: Nothing, because a green light gives you the right-of-way
c: Only the traffic light
d: Only oncoming cars turning left
exp: Before a right turn, check the crosswalk and look for riders coming up on your right.
src: California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (right of way)

q: A car in the lane next to you has stopped at a crosswalk. What should you do?
a: Keep going, because it may be stopped for its own reasons
b: Honk to see if someone is crossing
c: Stop, because someone may be crossing in front of it
d: Pass it carefully
exp: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A pedestrian may be hidden in front of it.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 6 (passing)

q: A pedestrian crosses in the middle of the block, away from any crosswalk. What must you do?
a: Keep going, because the pedestrian must yield
b: Slow down and stop if needed to avoid hitting the person
c: Honk and keep your speed
d: Speed up to pass before the person reaches your lane
exp: Even when a pedestrian should yield, drivers must take care to avoid hitting them.
src: California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (right of way)

q: When are you required to yield to pedestrians at an intersection with no painted crosswalk?
a: Only when a WALK signal is showing
b: Only when a crossing guard is present
c: When they are crossing in the unmarked crosswalk at the intersection
d: Never, because only painted crosswalks count
exp: Most intersections have unmarked crosswalks, and drivers yield there just as at marked ones.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (right of way)

q: An emergency vehicle has just passed you after you pulled over. What should you check before pulling back out?
a: Whether your hazard lights are on
b: Whether you can follow it closely
c: Whether the siren has stopped
d: Whether another emergency vehicle is following
exp: Emergency vehicles often travel in groups. Check before you move.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (emergency vehicles)

q: Which situation does a Move Over law cover?
a: A school bus with its yellow lights flashing
b: A car waiting to turn left
c: A funeral procession at an intersection
d: An emergency vehicle stopped beside the road with its lights flashing
exp: Move Over laws protect people working beside the road: move out of the next lane or slow down for a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing.
src: NHTSA, Move Over. It's the Law, https://www.nhtsa.gov/move-over-its-law

q: Passing a school bus that is stopped with its red lights flashing and its stop arm out is:
a: Allowed if no children are visible
b: Against the law
c: Allowed if you pass slowly
d: Allowed on the left side only
exp: Passing a school bus stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm out is against the law.
src: NHTSA, School Bus Safety, https://www.nhtsa.gov/road-safety/school-bus-safety

q: What does the stop arm on a school bus look like?
a: A yellow diamond on the back door
b: A red octagon that swings out from the left side of the bus
c: A green flag held by the driver
d: A white rectangle on the roof
exp: The stop arm is a red, eight sided sign that extends from the driver's side when the bus stops.
src: 49 CFR 571.131 (FMVSS 131, school bus stop signal arm); NHTSA, School Bus Safety, https://www.nhtsa.gov/road-safety/school-bus-safety

q: Where are children hardest for drivers to see near a stopped school bus?
a: Close to the bus, especially in front of it
b: Inside the bus
c: Far behind the bus
d: On the far sidewalk
exp: Children may cross in front of the bus or bend down near it, where drivers cannot see them well.
src: NHTSA, School Bus Safety, https://www.nhtsa.gov/road-safety/school-bus-safety

q: A city bus at a stop signals that it wants to pull back into traffic. What should you do?
a: Let it in when you safely can
b: Honk to warn the driver
c: Keep going, because the bus must wait for a gap
d: Speed up to pass it
exp: Letting a transit bus back into traffic is safe practice, and some states require it.
src: Official state driver manuals (yield to transit buses)

q: A funeral procession with headlights on is passing through an intersection. What should you do?
a: Wait for it to pass without cutting into the line
b: Join the end of the line to get through the light
c: Drive between the cars when your light is green
d: Pass the line on the left if that lane is clear
exp: Do not cut into, drive through or join a funeral procession. Wait until it has passed.
src: Official state driver manuals (funeral processions)

q: Another driver waves you through an intersection even though it is that driver's turn. What should you do?
a: Wait until the other driver goes anyway
b: Go right away, the driver has checked for you
c: Go slowly while watching only the driver who waved
d: Check for yourself that the way is clear before you go
exp: The other driver cannot see every lane or pedestrian for you. Look before you move.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (right of way)

q: An ambulance with its siren on passes you in heavy traffic. Should you pull in right behind it to get through faster?
a: No, stay well back; it may stop suddenly and others may follow
b: Yes, if you keep up with it
c: Yes, the siren clears the road for the cars behind it
d: Only until you are past the traffic jam
exp: Never follow an emergency vehicle closely: it may stop suddenly, and more emergency vehicles may be coming.
src: Uniform Vehicle Code (NCUTLO) 11-405 and 11-1107; PennDOT Driver's Manual, Chapter 3, https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmv/driver-services/pennsylvania-drivers-manual/online-drivers-manual/everyday-driving-skills/turning-merging-and-passing

q: Who has the right-of-way at a railroad crossing?
a: The train, always
b: The first vehicle to reach the tracks
c: The vehicle on the right
d: Cars, if the gates are up
exp: A train cannot stop or swerve quickly, so it always goes first.
src: Operation Lifesaver, safety tips for drivers, https://oli.org/site/nc/safety-tips

q: Traffic on the street you want to cross moves at about 30 mph. About how big a gap should you wait for before you turn left across it?
a: About 3 seconds
b: About 5 seconds
c: About 9 seconds
d: About 1 second
exp: A left turn across 30 mph traffic needs roughly 9 seconds of open space; crossing needs about 6 and a right turn about 8.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3, crossing and joining traffic; Montana OPI Driver Education, Gaps fact sheet (module 3.2)

q: Which of these means you need a bigger gap to cross or join traffic?
a: Traffic is moving faster than usual
b: The road is dry and level
c: Your car picks up speed quickly
d: Traffic is light
exp: Faster traffic, a wet road or a car that is slow to speed up all call for a bigger gap.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3; Montana OPI Driver Education, Gaps fact sheet (module 3.2)

q: You hear a siren but cannot tell where it is coming from. What should you do?
a: Keep your speed until you see the vehicle
b: Slow down and be ready to pull over
c: Stop at once in your lane
d: Speed up to clear the area
exp: Slow down and be ready to pull to the right until you know where the emergency vehicle is.
src: Uniform Vehicle Code (NCUTLO) 11-405; California Driver Handbook, https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/handbook/california-driver-handbook/

q: An emergency vehicle is coming. Where must you never stop when you pull over for it?
a: On the right shoulder
b: In an intersection
c: Next to the right curb
d: In an empty parking lane
exp: Never stop in an intersection; drive through it first, then pull to the right and stop.
src: Uniform Vehicle Code (NCUTLO) 11-405 (pull over clear of any intersection)

q: You are waiting to turn left, but a truck in the oncoming turn lane blocks your view of the lanes beyond it. What should you do?
a: Turn when the truck's driver waves you on
b: Wait until you can see every lane you must cross
c: Creep into the lanes and go if no one honks
d: Turn quickly so you spend less time in the lanes
exp: A left turner yields to oncoming traffic. If you cannot see every lane you must cross, you cannot know it is clear, so wait until you can.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3; Uniform Vehicle Code (NCUTLO) 11-402

q: When should you turn on your signal before a turn?
a: Just as you start to steer
b: Before you start slowing down, so drivers behind you know why you are braking
c: Once you are in the intersection
d: Only if a car is directly behind you
exp: Signal before you brake or begin the turn so others can plan for it.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (intersections and turns)

q: Your car stalls on the railroad tracks. What should you do first?
a: Get everyone out and away from the tracks right away
b: Stay in the car with your seat belt on
c: Push the car off the tracks
d: Try to restart the engine until it works
exp: Leave the vehicle immediately, even if no train is in sight.
src: Operation Lifesaver, safety tips for drivers, https://oli.org/site/nc/safety-tips

q: There is no stop line at a railroad crossing and a train is coming. What is the closest you may stop to the nearest rail?
a: 5 feet
b: 10 feet
c: 25 feet
d: 15 feet
exp: Stop no closer than 15 feet (and no more than 50 feet) from the nearest rail, because the train overhangs the rails.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 8C.03; 49 CFR 392.10; official state driver manuals

q: As you approach a roundabout, who has the right-of-way?
a: Traffic already in the roundabout
b: The driver on the right
c: Traffic waiting to enter
d: Whoever reaches the yield line first
exp: Entering drivers yield to vehicles already circulating.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 8 (roundabouts)

q: In which direction does traffic travel in a roundabout?
a: Counterclockwise, keeping the island on your right
b: Clockwise, keeping the island on your right
c: Counterclockwise, keeping the island on your left
d: Clockwise, keeping the island on your left
exp: In the United States, traffic in a roundabout travels counterclockwise.
src: California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (roundabouts)

q: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left while oncoming cars pass. How should your front wheels be pointed?
a: Straight ahead
b: Turned to the right
c: Turned to the right, away from oncoming traffic
d: It does not matter while your foot is on the brake
exp: If you are hit from behind with your wheels turned left, you will be pushed into oncoming traffic.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (intersections and turns)

q: You are turning left from a two way street onto another two way street. Which lane should you end in?
a: The lane just left of the center line
b: The far right lane
c: Any open lane on the new street
d: The lane just right of the center line
exp: Finish a left turn in the lane just right of the center line on the new road.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (intersections and turns)

q: You must slow down for a driveway where the driver behind you will not expect it. What should you do?
a: Turn on your hazard flashers and brake hard
b: Tap the brake pedal lightly a few times before you slow down
c: Brake firmly at the last moment so you stop quickly
d: Slow down without braking so your brake lights stay off
exp: A few light taps flash your brake lights and warn the driver behind you before an unexpected slowdown.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3, communicating with other drivers

q: In a two lane roundabout, which lane should you use to turn right at the first exit?
a: Either lane
b: The right lane
c: The left lane
d: The left lane, then move right inside the circle
exp: To turn right in a multi-lane roundabout, use the right lane.
src: California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (roundabouts)

q: A driver ahead has a left arm out the window, bent down at the elbow. What does it mean?
a: The driver is turning left
b: The driver is turning right
c: The driver wants you to pass
d: The driver is slowing down or stopping
exp: Arm bent down means slow or stop.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (hand signals); Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3 (hand signals)

q: When is the best time to slow down for a turn?
a: There is no need to slow down for a turn
b: After the turn is complete
c: In the middle of the turn
d: Before the turn, while your wheels are still straight
exp: Braking in the middle of a turn can upset the car. Slow down before you steer.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (intersections and turns)

q: You are making a right turn on a two lane road. Where should you start and end the turn?
a: Start close to the center line and end in any lane
b: Start in the left lane and end in the right lane
c: Swing wide to the left, then turn
d: Start close to the right edge and end in the right lane
exp: Right turns start and end as far right as practical. Avoid swinging wide.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (intersections and turns)

q: Why should you avoid swinging wide before a right turn?
a: A car or bicycle may slip into the gap on your right
b: It makes oncoming drivers think you are turning left
c: It makes your signal harder to see
d: It puts your rear wheels over the curb
exp: A wide swing leaves a gap on your right that other road users may enter.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (intersections and turns)

q: An oncoming car has its right turn signal on while you wait to turn left. What should you do?
a: Wait until you are sure the car is really turning
b: Turn once the car starts to slow
c: Turn right away, because it is turning
d: Wait for it only if it is a large vehicle
exp: Do not assume a signaling driver will turn. Wait until the car starts its turn.
src: California Driver Handbook, Navigating the Roads (left turns)

q: You are on a one way street and want to turn left onto another one way street. Which lane should you start in?
a: Any lane, if you signal
b: The center lane
c: The far left lane
d: The far right lane
exp: On a one way street, a left turn starts from the lane nearest the left curb.
src: California Driver Handbook, Navigating the Roads (turns)

q: You are turning left from a two way street onto a one way street. Which lane should you start in?
a: The shoulder
b: The far right lane
c: The lane nearest the center of the road
d: The parking lane
exp: From a two way street, a left turn starts in the lane next to the center line.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (intersections and turns)

q: You are in the inner of two left turn lanes. Where should you end your turn?
a: In whichever lane is empty
b: In the outer lane, crossing the other turning car's path
c: In the far right lane
d: In the matching inner lane on the new road
exp: In a multi-lane turn, each lane turns into its matching lane. Stay in your lane through the turn.
src: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3 (dual left turn lanes); MUTCD 11th ed., Section 3B.23 (lane-use arrows)

q: You want to turn right across a bike lane, and a cyclist is riding in it beside you. What should you do?
a: Let the cyclist pass, then turn
b: Turn first, the cyclist must yield
c: Speed up to get ahead of the cyclist
d: Turn in front of the cyclist if you signaled first
exp: A cyclist going straight in the bike lane has the right-of-way over a turning driver.
src: California Driver Handbook, Navigating the Roads (bike lanes)

q: Where is a U-turn almost never allowed?
a: On a quiet residential street with clear views
b: Near a curve or hilltop where other drivers cannot see you
c: In a large empty parking lot
d: At a wide intersection with no NO U-TURN sign
exp: U-turns are dangerous where drivers cannot see you in time.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (U-turns)

q: Which of these places is a U-turn not allowed?
a: At a median opening with no sign against it
b: On a railroad crossing
c: At a wide residential street with clear views
d: In a driveway turnaround
exp: U-turns are not allowed on or at railroad crossings.
src: California Driver Handbook, Navigating the Roads (U-turns)

q: What is the first step of a three-point turn?
a: Shift to reverse
b: Back up into a driveway
c: Signal right, pull to the right edge and stop
d: Turn the wheel sharply left and drive forward
exp: A three-point turn begins at the right edge, then you check traffic and turn left across the road.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (three-point turn)

q: During a three-point turn, after you pull forward across the road and stop, what do you do next?
a: Drive forward over the curb
b: Check traffic, turn the wheel sharply right and back up slowly
c: Turn the wheel left and back up
d: Turn on your hazard lights and wait
exp: The second move is backing up with the wheel turned right, stopping before the curb.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (three-point turn)

q: You missed your exit in a roundabout. What should you do?
a: Cut across the center island
b: Go around again to your exit
c: Stop and back up
d: Take the next exit and make a U-turn on the ramp
exp: Keep moving and take another lap. Stopping or backing up in the circle is dangerous.
src: California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (roundabouts)

q: In a two lane roundabout, which lane should you use to go back the way you came?
a: Either lane, changing lanes as needed
b: The left lane
c: The truck apron
d: The right lane
exp: Use the left lane for a left turn or a U-turn, and stay in it until you exit.
src: California Driver Handbook, Laws and Rules of the Road (roundabouts)

q: When should you signal in a roundabout?
a: Never signal in a roundabout
b: Signal right as soon as you enter
c: Signal right just before your exit
d: Signal left the whole way around
exp: Signal right as you approach your exit so others know you are leaving.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 8 (roundabouts)

q: Why should you not drive beside a large truck in a roundabout?
a: Trucks have the right-of-way over cars in a roundabout
b: Trucks must stop in the roundabout
c: The truck may need more than one lane to get around
d: Trucks must leave at the first exit
exp: Large vehicles may use the truck apron and more than one lane, so give them room.
src: Minnesota DOT, Roundabouts: large trucks; Wisconsin DOT roundabout brochure; FHWA-SA-14-098

q: What does a driver's left arm held straight out the window mean?
a: You may pass on the left
b: Slow down or stop
c: A left turn
d: A right turn
exp: Arm straight out means a left turn.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (hand signals); Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3 (hand signals)

q: What does a driver's left arm held out and bent up at the elbow mean?
a: Pull over
b: Slow down or stop
c: A left turn
d: A right turn
exp: Arm bent up means a right turn.
src: New York State Driver's Manual, Chapter 5 (hand signals); Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3 (hand signals)

q: You are out of a car stalled on the tracks and a train is coming. Which way should you move?
a: Toward the train, away from the tracks at an angle
b: In the same direction the train is moving
c: Straight down the tracks
d: Back into the car
exp: Debris is thrown forward in the direction the train travels, so move toward the train and away at an angle.
src: Operation Lifesaver, safety tips for drivers, https://oli.org/site/nc/safety-tips

q: What is the blue sign at a railroad crossing for?
a: Showing the detour route if the crossing is blocked
b: Calling the railroad to report a problem, such as a stalled car
c: Showing the distance to the next crossing
d: Telling you the crossing has gates
exp: The Emergency Notification System sign shows a phone number and crossing ID number.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 8B.27

q: A train has just passed at a crossing with two tracks. The gates are still down. What should you do?
a: Wait, because another train may be coming on the other track
b: Cross as soon as the first train clears the road
c: Drive around the gates now
d: Go if you cannot see another train
exp: A second train can be hidden by the first. Wait until the gates rise and the lights stop.
src: Pennsylvania Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3 (railroad crossings); Operation Lifesaver, safety tips for drivers, https://oli.org/site/nc/safety-tips

q: When is a quick, light tap of the horn the right choice?
a: A child near the road looks about to run into your path
b: The driver ahead is slow to go on a green light
c: Another driver has just cut you off
d: You are passing a cyclist
exp: A light tap warns someone who has not seen you; the horn is never for anger or to hurry others.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3; California Driver Handbook, https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/handbook/california-driver-handbook/

q: When should you use a long, firm blast of the horn?
a: When a driver cuts you off and you want them to know
b: To ask a slow driver to speed up
c: Every time you pass a cyclist
d: When you are in real danger, such as a car about to hit you
exp: Save a long blast for real danger; never honk out of anger, and avoid honking near cyclists.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3; California Driver Handbook, https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/handbook/california-driver-handbook/

q: When should you turn on your hazard flashers?
a: When you park briefly in a no parking zone
b: When you are following another car closely
c: When your car is stopped on or beside the road
d: When you drive slowly in heavy rain
exp: Hazard flashers warn others that your car is stopped or disabled on or beside the road.
src: Uniform Vehicle Code (NCUTLO); California Driver Handbook, https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/handbook/california-driver-handbook/

q: You want to pull out in front of a driver waiting at a stop sign. How can you best tell the driver has seen you?
a: Try to make eye contact; if the driver has not looked at you, assume you are not seen
b: The driver's turn signal is on
c: The car's headlights are on
d: The car is stopped, so the driver must have seen you
exp: Eye contact is the best sign that a driver, cyclist or pedestrian has seen you.
src: California Driver Handbook, https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/handbook/california-driver-handbook/ (Safe Driving)

q: When you turn, how do your rear wheels move compared with your front wheels?
a: They follow exactly the same path
b: They swing wider than the front wheels
c: They cut inside the path of the front wheels
d: They stay straight until the turn ends
exp: Rear wheels off-track: they follow a shorter path inside the front wheels, so a tight right turn can put a rear tire on the curb.
src: FMCSA/state CDL manuals on off-tracking; California Driver Handbook, https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/handbook/california-driver-handbook/

q: As a general guide, about how long before a turn should you turn on your signal?
a: About 1 second
b: About 10 seconds
c: About 3 to 4 seconds
d: Only once you start to steer
exp: About 3 to 4 seconds of warning lets drivers behind you see why you are slowing. Your state also sets a minimum distance.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3 (signaling)

q: Which of these is a good reason to use your horn?
a: To tell a slow driver to hurry
b: To greet a friend on the sidewalk
c: To get a cyclist to move over
d: To warn others when you have lost control of your car
exp: Use the horn to warn of danger, including when you have lost control of your car. Never honk out of anger or at cyclists.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual (PUB 95), Chapter 3 (horn); Uniform Vehicle Code (NCUTLO) 12-401

q: The posted limit is 45 mph, but heavy rain makes it hard to see the road ahead. What speed does the basic speed law require?
a: Exactly 45 mph
b: A speed that is safe for the rain and the distance you can see
c: Any speed up to 45 mph
d: The posted minimum speed, so you do not block traffic
exp: The basic speed law says you may never drive faster than is safe for current conditions, even when you are under the posted limit.
src: State basic speed law; NHTSA Speeding, https://www.nhtsa.gov/risky-driving/speeding

q: If you double your speed, about how much longer is your braking distance?
a: About the same
b: About twice as long
c: About four times as long
d: About three times as long
exp: Braking distance grows with the square of speed, so twice the speed needs about four times the distance to brake.
src: State driver manuals, stopping distance

q: What is the best way to measure your following distance?
a: Keep one car length for every 10 mph of speed
b: Stay back far enough to read the car's license plate
c: Count the seconds between the car ahead and you passing a fixed point
d: Keep a gap of about 20 feet at any speed
exp: Pick a fixed object; when the car ahead passes it, count until you reach it. A time gap grows as your speed grows.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual, Managing Space, https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmv/driver-services/pennsylvania-drivers-manual/online-drivers-manual/everyday-driving-skills/managing-space

q: About how far ahead should you look when you drive?
a: About 2 to 3 seconds ahead
b: About 4 seconds ahead, the same as your following distance
c: About 6 to 8 seconds ahead
d: At least 12 to 15 seconds ahead
exp: Look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead, about a block or more in the city or a quarter mile on the highway, so you find problems early.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual, Managing Space, https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmv/driver-services/pennsylvania-drivers-manual/online-drivers-manual/everyday-driving-skills/managing-space; California Driver Handbook, Safe Driving, https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/handbook/california-driver-handbook/safe-driving/

q: A driver is tailgating you. What is the safest thing to do?
a: Slam on your brakes to warn the driver
b: Speed up to get away
c: Pull onto the shoulder and stop right away
d: Move to the right lane if you can and let the driver pass
exp: Letting a tailgater pass removes the danger behind you. Sudden braking can cause a rear end crash.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual, Managing Space, https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmv/driver-services/pennsylvania-drivers-manual/online-drivers-manual/everyday-driving-skills/managing-space

q: When should you slow down for a sharp curve?
a: In the middle of the curve, where it is sharpest
b: Before the curve, while the car is still going straight
c: As you come out of the curve
d: Only if a yellow advisory speed plaque is posted
exp: Slow down before the curve; braking hard in the curve can make the tires lose their grip.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual, Chapter 3, Managing Space, https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmv/driver-services/pennsylvania-drivers-manual/online-drivers-manual/everyday-driving-skills/managing-space; California Driver Handbook, https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/handbook/california-driver-handbook/

q: In which situation should you leave more following distance than normal?
a: When following a large truck that blocks your view
b: On a freeway in light traffic
c: When the car ahead is a small, light car
d: When you are driving a little below the limit
exp: Large vehicles block your view of the road ahead, so you need more room to see and react.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual, Managing Space, https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmv/driver-services/pennsylvania-drivers-manual/online-drivers-manual/everyday-driving-skills/managing-space

q: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
a: Check your inside mirror only
b: Turn your head and look over your shoulder
c: Rely on your side mirror only
d: Rely on your blind spot warning light
exp: Mirrors leave blind spots. A quick look over your shoulder through the side window is the only full check.
src: PennDOT Driver's Manual, Managing Space, https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmv/driver-services/pennsylvania-drivers-manual/online-drivers-manual/everyday-driving-skills/managing-space

q: Which three parts add up to your total stopping distance?
a: Perception distance, reaction distance and braking distance
b: Following distance, braking distance and skid distance
c: Reaction distance, braking distance and skid distance
d: Sight distance, passing distance and braking distance
exp: Total stopping distance is the distance traveled while you notice the hazard, while your foot moves to the brake, and while the brakes stop the car.
src: NHTSA and state driver manuals, stopping distance

q: What does the number on a white Speed Limit sign tell you?
a: The speed you must drive
b: The lowest speed allowed
c: The suggested speed for curves
d: The highest legal speed in good conditions
exp: A posted limit is a ceiling for good conditions, not a target. Bad conditions call for a lower speed.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2B.21

q: Can you get a ticket for speeding while driving below the posted limit?
a: No, never
b: Only on a freeway
c: Yes, if your speed is too fast for the conditions
d: Only at night
exp: Under the basic speed law, an officer can cite you for driving too fast for weather, traffic or road conditions even below the limit.
src: State basic speed law; NHTSA Speeding, https://www.nhtsa.gov/risky-driving/speeding

q: Why can driving far below the speed of other traffic be dangerous?
a: Other drivers bunch up behind you and make risky passes
b: It wears out your brakes
c: It uses more fuel
d: It is never dangerous
